rounds.text: The valuation of India Cements Capital Ltd is heavily stretched, with the stock trading at a price-to-book multiple of 3.38x against a sector benchmark of just 1.23x [E1, E6]. This elevated multiple rests on deeply negative underlying profitability, evidenced by a trailing twelve-month profit growth collapse of -267% and a current ROE of -0.8% [E12, E18]. Long-term value creation is practically non-existent, highlighted by a stagnant 10-year compounded sales contraction of -35% and a meager 10-year median return on equity of 2% [E13, E23]. Operational risks are further compounded by severe working capital bloat, specifically high debtors stretching to 198 days, alongside a flagged low interest coverage ratio [E41, E43]. Most critically, insiders are fleeing the equity; promoter holding has plummeted by 24.88 percentage points from 74.90% in December 2023 down to 50.02% by September 2026 [E33]. Conceded: [E28] and [E29] show the company generated positive operating and free cash flow of Rs 41.33 Cr and Rs 41.32 Cr respectively in March 2026.
